Title: Fundamentals of Differential Equations, Eighth Edition

Author: R. Kent Nagle

Chapter: 7.3

Question: 1

Because of the linearity property of the Laplace transform, [;\mathcal{L}\{{t^2} + {e^t}\}=\mathcal{L}\{t^2\} + \mathcal{L}\{e^t\sin2t\};].

Using the fact that [;\mathcal{L}\{t^n\}=\frac{n!}{s^{n+1}};] (from a table), [;\mathcal{L}\{t^2\}=\frac{2!}{s^{2+1}}=\frac{2}{s^3};].

Employing the first shifting theorem,

[;\mathcal{L}\{e^{at}f(t)\}=F(s-a);]

[;\mathcal{L}\{e^t\sin2t\}=\mathcal{L}\{e^tf(t)\};]

[;\mathcal{L}\{f(t)\}=\mathcal{L}\{\sin2t\}=\frac{2}{s^2+2^2}=\frac{2}{s^2+4};] (using [;\mathcal{L}\{\sin{at}\}=\frac{a}{s^2+a^2};], from a table).

So, [;\mathcal{L}\{e^t\sin2t\}=F(s-1)=\frac{2}{(s-1)^2+4};].

Substituting these back into the original, [;\mathcal{L}\{{t^2} + {e^t}\}=\mathcal{L}\{t^2\} + \mathcal{L}\{e^t\sin2t\}=\frac{2}{s^3} + \frac{2}{(s-1)^2+4};].

Therefore, [;\mathcal{L}\{{t^2} + {e^t}\}=\frac{2}{s^3} + \frac{2}{(s-1)^2+4};].

I am an Army veteran and Afghanistan war veteran who has been out for 3 years now, AMA!

What was your job when you were in the army and did you enjoy your job? Any awesome or hilarious stories from basic training? Everyone seems to have hilarious stories about drill sergeants or at least interesting ones. Also what do you do now for a job or what's your current job goals?

What was your job when you were in the army and did you enjoy your job?

My official job was Systems Support Specialist (IT) However I was attached to an Infantry Battalion and later thrown down to the company level where I was a radio operator for the line guys. I assisted in everything radio-wise for a company of about 70-100 infantrymen. I enjoyed it because I was able to have an office job while at the same time able to go out on patrols and missions multiple times a week. It was very stressful at the time but extremely rewarding to see my hard work making a difference.

Basic training stories

Funny enough that I do have one. One morning towards the end of basic I was especially tired and exhausted in the chow line waiting for breakfast. There was a custom of yelling "MAKE A HOLE" when a drill sergeant or member of the cadre were coming in your path. Everyone would shove and shuffle at the speed of light to get out of the way and essentially make a pathway for the drill sergeant. On this particular day, for reasons beyond my understanding, I yelled "MAKE A BIG HOLE" at one of the stockier staff sergeant drill sergeants. He stopped in his tracks and stared me right in the eyes and said "You are damned lucky I am hungry private" and made his way to the chow line. He ended up calling me out later in the day and we "exercised" in the sand pit for an hour or two.

What do I do now

I am a Sr. Systems Administrator for an international shipping company. I actually just started this job, came over as a Tech Lead and Project Manager for a managed services IT company. So for now my current job goals are to transition into this new role and hope for the best! Thank you for your questions!

Oh man. I can just imagine what went through his head when you yelled that at him.

That's really cool, good luck at your new job! I think most everyone forgets how much of the military is probably just general labor/tech work instead of soldiering (I'm just gonna use that as a verb because I can't think of a better way to describe it...).

After being at war, what is your opinion on them? Do you believe they should be continued, expanded, made smaller, or ended altogether? EDIT: Also, because we've got to know, what's your favorite flavor of ice cream?

I'd rather there not be war at all. While I understand that in some circumstances war is unavoidable, usually for one party/side, but the wars we are waging these days are pointless.

Ice cream: Vanilla with chocolate syrup "Super plain... i know"
Thanks. I think we just need to leave because we're making it worse for the most part. Also, your choice in ice cream is good.

I put all of my eggs in that basket and it ended up biting me in the ass after the company suffered some hardships and started freezing new hires.

Can you give some examples of what your missions were? Assist a team to repair a radio tower or escort or what?

I was in an infantry unit, missions were primarily of an infantry nature. We did air assault missions to clear and disrupt supply routes on the Afghan-Pakistan border often. Many times we did "show of force" to scatter taliban out of a civilian area.
Any advice for a soon to be airborne 68 Whiskey (medic for those of you who don't know)

Pay attention to your studies in AIT and treat the experience as a learning one rather than a partying one. Many people fail out of 68W school. We had nearly an entire platoon of 68W reclass soldiers who couldn't pass the school and switched MOS to ours.

As for airborne, make sure you are ready to run. You will be running everywhere.

There were also a bunch of 25U failures that went to 68W school. When I was in airborne school there was a guy that had already been in for two years and reclassed twice due to being an idiot. He went from some MI mos to 74D to 11B and managed to pick up a slot for airborne via option 40.

Also, in addition to running well make sure you can run far.
